sentences.zh: 孔靖

translations.literal: Kong Jing
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jing

sentences.zh: 孔靖字季恭，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Jing, style name Jigong, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jing, whose style name was Jigong, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 名與高祖祖諱同，故稱字。

translations.literal: His personal name matched the taboo of Gaozu's grandfather, so he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his given name matched the taboo on Gaozu's grandfather's name, he was addressed by his style name instead.

sentences.zh: 祖愉，晉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu had been Cavalry General-in-Chief under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had served Jin as Cavalry General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 父誾，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Yin had been Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had been Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 季恭始察郡孝廉，功曹史，著作佐郎，太子舍人，鎮軍司馬，司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Jigong was first nominated as commandery Filial and Incorrupt, then served as chief clerk, aide in the Bureau of Composition, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, army aide on the Pacification Army staff, and western clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Jigong was nominated as a commandery Filial and Incorrupt candidate and held posts as chief clerk, aide in the Bureau of Composition, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, army aide on the Pacification Army staff, and western clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遭母憂。

translations.literal: Before he could take office, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his appointment, he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 隆安五年，於喪中被起建威將軍、山陰令，不就。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Long'an, while still in mourning he was summoned to the posts of General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Shanyin, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Long'an he was recalled from mourning to serve as General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Shanyin, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，屢至會稽，季恭曲意禮接，贍給甚厚。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched east against Sun En and repeatedly came to Kuaiji, Jigong received him with every courtesy and supplied him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned east against Sun En and repeatedly passed through Kuaiji, Jigong treated him with elaborate courtesy and supported him very generously.

sentences.zh: 高祖後討孫恩，時桓玄篡形已著，欲於山陰建義討之。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu campaigned again against Sun En, Huan Xuan's usurpation was already plain, and Gaozu wished to raise arms at Shanyin to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: On a later campaign against Sun En, Huan Xuan's usurpation was already obvious, and Gaozu planned to raise a righteous force at Shanyin to overthrow him.

sentences.zh: 季恭以為山陰去京邑路遠，且玄未居極位，不如待其篡逆事彰，釁成惡稔，徐於京口圖之，不憂不剋。

translations.literal: Jigong held that Shanyin was far from the capital by road, and that since Xuan had not yet reached the supreme position, it would be better to wait until his treason was fully exposed, guilt ripened, and evil fully formed, then slowly plot at Jingkou—there would be no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Jigong argued that Shanyin was too far from the capital, and that since Xuan had not yet seized the throne outright, they should wait until his usurpation was fully exposed and his crimes fully ripened, then move deliberately from Jingkou—success would be assured.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦謂為然。

translations.literal: Gaozu also thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 虞嘯父為征東將軍、會稽內史，季恭初求為府司馬，不得。

translations.literal: Yu Xiaofu was General Who Conquers the East and Interior Governor of Kuaiji; Jigong had first sought to become his staff major but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu held the posts of General Who Conquers the East and Interior Governor of Kuaiji. Jigong had earlier sought a post as major on his staff but was turned down.

sentences.zh: 及帝定桓玄，以季恭為內史，使齎封板拜授，正與季恭相值，季恭便回舟夜還。

translations.literal: When the emperor had settled Huan Xuan, Jigong was made Interior Governor; an envoy was sent bearing sealed appointment boards to invest him. He happened to meet Jigong on the way, and Jigong turned his boat about and returned that same night.
translations.idiomatic: After the court had suppressed Huan Xuan, Jigong was appointed Interior Governor and an envoy was dispatched with sealed boards of appointment. He met Jigong on the route; Jigong at once turned his boat and returned by night.

sentences.zh: 至即叩扉告嘯父，并令掃拂別齋，即便入郡。

translations.literal: On arrival he knocked at the gate to inform Xiaofu, ordered a separate lodging swept, and immediately entered the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived he knocked at Xiaofu's gate to announce himself, had a separate lodging cleaned, and entered the commandery administration at once.

sentences.zh: 嘯父本為桓玄所授，聞玄敗，震懼，開門請罪。

translations.literal: Xiaofu had originally been appointed by Huan Xuan; hearing of Xuan's defeat, he was terrified and opened his gate to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofu had originally been appointed by Huan Xuan. When he heard of Xuan's defeat he was terrified and opened his gate to plead guilty.

sentences.zh: 季恭慰勉，使且安所住，明旦乃移。

translations.literal: Jigong comforted and encouraged him, telling him to remain where he was for the time being and move only the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: Jigong comforted him and told him to stay where he was for the night and move only the next morning.

sentences.zh: 季恭到任，務存治實，敕止浮華，翦罰遊惰，由是寇盜衰止，境內肅清。

translations.literal: Once in office, Jigong devoted himself to solid governance, forbade empty display, and punished idleness and wandering; banditry dwindled and stopped, and the district was brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: In office Jigong pursued practical administration, forbade ostentation, and punished idleness and vagrancy. Banditry declined and ceased, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 徵為右衞將軍，加給事中，不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of the Right Guard with added status as Supernumerary Palace Attendant, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of the Right Guard with added status as Supernumerary Palace Attendant, but declined.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，領本國中正，徙琅邪王大司馬司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant and head of his native state's chief rectifier, then transferred as major on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and head of his native state's chief rectifier, then transferred as major on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 尋出為吳興太守，加冠軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as Administrator of Wuxing with the additional title Champion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Administrator of Wuxing with the additional title Champion.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳興頻喪太守，云項羽神為卞山王，居郡聽事，二千石至，常避之，季恭居聽事，竟無害也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wuxing had repeatedly lost its administrators; it was said that the spirit of Xiang Yu, as King of Bianshan, dwelt in the commandery hall, and when a two-thousand-bushel official arrived he always avoided it. Jigong occupied the hall and suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Wuxing had lost one administrator after another. People said the spirit of Xiang Yu, as King of Bianshan, dwelt in the commandery hall and that incoming two-thousand-bushel officials always avoided it. Jigong took up residence in the hall and came to no harm.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，固讓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，復督五郡諸軍、征虜、會稽內史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi he again supervised military affairs in five commanderies and served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yixi he again supervised military affairs in five commanderies and served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 修飾學校，督課誦習。

translations.literal: He restored the schools and supervised study and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He refurbished the schools and supervised study and recitation.

sentences.zh: 十年，復為尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，又讓不拜。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again made Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Leads the Army with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Leads the Army with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 十二年，致仕，拜金紫光錄大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he retired from office and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with recording duties, retaining his attendant status.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he retired and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with recording duties, retaining his attendant status.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高祖北伐，季恭求從，以為太尉軍諮祭酒、後將軍。

translations.literal: That year, when Gaozu marched north, Jigong asked to accompany the campaign and was made consultation army aide on the Grand Commandant's staff and Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Gaozu marched north, Jigong asked to join the campaign and was appointed consultation army aide on the Grand Commandant's staff and Rear General.

sentences.zh: 從平關、洛。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Guanzhong and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為相國，又隨府遷。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Jigong moved with the office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Jigong transferred with the office.

sentences.zh: 宋臺初建，令書以為尚書令，加散騎常侍，又讓不受，乃拜侍中、特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Song regime was first established, an imperial order named him Minister of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry; he again declined and would not accept, and was then appointed Palace Attendant, Special Grand Master, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song regime was first established, an imperial order named him Minister of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry. He declined again and was instead appointed Palace Attendant, Special Grand Master, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.

sentences.zh: 辭事東歸，高祖餞之戲馬臺，百僚咸賦詩以述其美。

translations.literal: He resigned his duties and returned east; Gaozu feasted him at Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the hundred officials all composed poems to praise his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned east. Gaozu gave him a farewell feast at the Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the hundred officials all composed poems in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 及受命，加開府儀同三司，辭讓累年，終以不受。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Jigong was offered the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes; he declined for years and in the end never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the Mandate, he was offered the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes. He declined for years and never accepted.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，薨，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: Section marker.

sentences.zh: 子 山士

translations.literal: Son: Shanshi
translations.idiomatic: (Son Shanshi)

sentences.zh: =子山士，歷顯位，侍中，會稽太守，坐小弟駕部郎道穰逼略良家子女，白衣領郡。

translations.literal: =His son Shanshi rose through eminent posts to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Kuaiji. Because his younger brother, Master of Coaches Dao Rang, had coerced and seized children of good families, he held the commandery in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanshi rose through eminent posts to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Kuaiji. Because his younger brother, Master of Coaches Dao Rang, had coerced and seized children of good families, Shanshi was reduced to administering the commandery in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he died in office.

translations.literal: Section marker.

sentences.zh: 子 靈符

translations.literal: Younger brother: Lingfu
translations.idiomatic: (Younger brother Lingfu)

sentences.zh: =弟靈符，元嘉末，為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: =His younger brother Lingfu, at the end of Yuanjia, served as chief administrator on the Minister of Works staff of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, and as Administrator of Nan commandery and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lingfu, at the end of Yuanjia, served as chief administrator on the Minister of Works staff of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, and as Administrator of Nan commandery and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明初，自侍中為輔國將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daming era under Shizu, he left the post of Palace Attendant to become General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daming era under Shizu, he left the post of Palace Attendant to become General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 山陰縣土境褊狹，民多田少，靈符表徙無貲之家於餘姚、鄞、鄮三縣界，墾起湖田。

translations.literal: The territory of Shanyin county was narrow and cramped, with many people and little land. Lingfu memorialized to move households without means to the borders of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and to open lake fields for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin county was cramped, with many people and little land. Lingfu memorialized to move impoverished households to the borders of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and to open lake fields for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 上使公卿博議，太宰江夏王義恭議曰：「夫訓農修本，有國所同，土著之民，習翫日久，如京師無田，不聞徙居他縣。

translations.literal: The emperor had the high ministers debate the matter at length. Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, argued: "Training the people in agriculture and repairing the foundations are alike for every state. Natives long settled grow used to their ways over time; in the capital, when people have no fields, one does not hear of moving them to other counties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the high ministers debate the proposal at length. Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, argued: "Teaching agriculture and strengthening the foundations are the same for every state. Long-settled natives grow attached to their ways over time; in the capital, when people lack fields, one never hears of relocating them to other counties.

sentences.zh: 尋山陰豪族富室，頃畝不少，貧者肆力，非為無處，耕起空荒，無救災歉。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Shanyin the great clans and wealthy houses hold no small acreage; the poor can exert their strength—there is not truly no place for them. Opening empty waste land will not relieve famine and shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in Shanyin the great clans and wealthy houses hold considerable land; the poor can still work—they are not truly without a place. Opening empty waste land will not relieve famine and shortage.

sentences.zh: 又緣湖居民，魚鴨為業，及有居肆，理無樂徙。

translations.literal: Again, lakeside residents make their living from fish and ducks, and some keep shops; by reason they cannot be glad to move.
translations.idiomatic: Again, lakeside residents live by fish and ducks, and some keep shops; by rights they cannot welcome relocation.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令柳元景、右僕射劉秀之、尚書王瓚之、顧凱之、顏師伯、嗣湘東王彧議曰：「富戶溫房，無假遷業；

translations.literal: " Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Vice Minister of the Right Liu Xiuzhi, and Ministers Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir-designate Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, argued: "Wealthy households in warm rooms need not change their livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Vice Minister of the Right Liu Xiuzhi, and Ministers Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir-designate Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, argued: "Wealthy households in warm rooms need not change their livelihood;

sentences.zh: 窮身寒室，必應徙居。

translations.literal: those in poor bodies and cold rooms must be moved.
translations.idiomatic: those in poor bodies and cold rooms must be moved.

sentences.zh: 葺宇疏臯，產粒無待，資公則公未易充，課私則私卒難具。

translations.literal: They build houses on sparse marshland and cannot wait for grain; if the state must supply them, the state cannot easily fill the need; if private households must provide, private households can hardly furnish it.
translations.idiomatic: They would build houses on sparse marshland and could not wait for grain. If the state must supply them, the state cannot easily meet the need; if private households must provide, private households can hardly furnish it.

sentences.zh: 生計既完，畬功自息，宜募亡叛通卹及與樂田者，其往經創，須粗修立，然後徙居。

translations.literal: Once livelihoods are secure, the work of clearing fields will cease of itself. One should recruit fugitives and rebels under amnesty and those who delight in farming; where the land has suffered harm, it must first be roughly repaired, and only then should people be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Once livelihoods are secure, the work of clearing fields will cease of itself. One should recruit fugitives and rebels under amnesty and those who delight in farming; where the land has suffered harm, it must first be roughly repaired, and only then should people be moved.

sentences.zh: 」侍中沈懷文、王景文、黃門侍郎劉敳、郄顒議曰：「百姓雖不親農，不無資生之路，若驅以就田，則坐相違奪。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Liu Yi and Qie Yan argued: "Though the common people do not personally farm, they are not without ways to make a living; if they are driven onto the fields, their livelihoods will simply be seized from them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Liu Yi and Qie Yan argued: "Though common people do not personally farm, they are not without ways to make a living; if they are driven onto the fields, their livelihoods will simply be seized from them.

sentences.zh: 且鄞等三縣，去治並遠，既安之民，忽徙他邑，新垣未立，舊居已毀，去留兩困，無以自資。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yin and the other three counties are far from the seat of government. People already settled, if suddenly moved to another district, will find new walls not yet built and old dwellings already destroyed—troubled whether to go or stay, with no means to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yin and the other three counties are far from the seat of government. People already settled, if suddenly moved to another district, will find new walls not yet built and old dwellings already destroyed—troubled whether to go or stay, with no means to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 謂宜適任民情，從其所樂，開宥逋亡，且令就業，若審成腴壤，然後議遷。

translations.literal: They held that one should suit the people's feelings, let them follow what they enjoy, pardon fugitives, and for the time being let them take up their trades; if the land is truly shown to be fertile, then one may discuss relocation.
translations.idiomatic: They held that one should suit the people's feelings, let them follow what they enjoy, pardon fugitives, and for the time being let them take up their trades; if the land is truly shown to be fertile, then one may discuss relocation.

sentences.zh: 」太常王玄謨議曰：「小民貧匱，遠就荒疇，去舊即新，糧種俱闕，習之既難，勸之未易。

translations.literal: " Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Small people are poor and destitute; sent far to waste land, leaving the old for the new, grain and seed alike lacking—hard to accustom them, and hard to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Small people are poor and destitute; sent far to waste land, leaving the old for the new, grain and seed alike lacking—hard to accustom them, and hard to encourage them.

sentences.zh: 謂宜微加資給，使得肆勤，明力田之賞，申怠惰之罰。

translations.literal: They held that one should add a little support so that they could exert themselves, make clear rewards for diligent farming, and enforce penalties for idleness.
translations.idiomatic: They held that one should add a little support so that they could exert themselves, make clear rewards for diligent farming, and enforce penalties for idleness.

sentences.zh: 」光祿勳王昇之議曰：「遠廢之疇，方翦荊棘，率課窮乏，其事彌難，資徙粗立，徐行無晚。

translations.literal: " Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Sheng argued: "On distant abandoned fields one is only now cutting brambles; to drive the poor to labor there is all the harder. Let support for relocation be roughly established first; there is no harm in proceeding slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Sheng argued: "On distant abandoned fields one is only now cutting brambles; to drive the poor to labor there is all the harder. Let support for relocation be roughly established first; there is no harm in proceeding slowly.

sentences.zh: 」上違議，從其徙民，並成良業。

translations.literal: " The emperor rejected the debates and followed the plan to move the people; all became good cultivators.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the debates and followed the plan to move the people; all became good cultivators.

sentences.zh: 靈符自丹陽出為會稽太守，尋加豫章王子尚撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Lingfu left Danyang to become Administrator of Kuaiji, and soon was added as chief administrator on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, Zishang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu left Danyang to become Administrator of Kuaiji, and soon was added as chief administrator on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, Zishang.

sentences.zh: 靈符家本豐，產業甚廣，又於永興立墅，周回三十三里，水陸地二百六十五頃，含帶二山，又有果園九處。

translations.literal: Lingfu's family was originally wealthy and his estates very broad; he also established a manor at Yongxing, thirty-three li in circuit, with two hundred sixty-five qing of land by water and land embracing two hills, and nine orchards besides.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu's family was originally wealthy and his estates very broad. He also established a manor at Yongxing, thirty-three li in circuit, with two hundred sixty-five qing of land by water and land embracing two hills, and nine orchards besides.

sentences.zh: 為有司所糾，詔原之，而靈符答對不實，坐以免官。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the responsible officials; an edict pardoned him, but because Lingfu's replies were untrue he was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by the responsible officials. An edict pardoned him, but because Lingfu's replies were untrue he was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 後復舊官，又為尋陽王子房右軍長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: Later he was restored to his former post and also served as chief administrator on the Right Army staff of the Prince of Xunyang, Zifang, while retaining his post as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was restored to his former post and also served as chief administrator on the Right Army staff of the Prince of Xunyang, Zifang, while retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 慤實有材幹，不存華飾，每所蒞官，政績修理。

translations.literal: Steadfast and capable, he kept no empty display; in every office he held, administration was well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and capable, he kept no empty display; in every office he held, administration was well ordered.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和中，犯忤近臣，為所讒搆，遣鞭殺之。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, in the Jinghe era, he offended a close minister and was slandered by him; he was sent to be beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, in the Jinghe era, he offended a close minister and was slandered by him; he was sent to be beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 二子湛之、淵之，於都賜死。

translations.literal: His two sons, Zhanzhi and Yuanzhi, were granted death in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Zhanzhi and Yuanzhi, were granted death in the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追贈靈符金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Lingfu was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Lingfu was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 淵之大明中為尚書比部郎。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi, in the Daming era, served as Director of the Review Bureau in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi, in the Daming era, served as Director of the Review Bureau in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時安陸應城縣民張江陵與妻吳共罵母黃令死，黃忿恨自經死，值赦。

translations.literal: At the time, Zhang Jiangling of Yingcheng county in Anlu and his wife Wu together reviled his mother Huang until she died; Huang, in resentment, hanged herself. An amnesty was in force.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Zhang Jiangling of Yingcheng county in Anlu and his wife Wu together reviled his mother Huang until she died; Huang, in resentment, hanged herself. An amnesty was in force.

sentences.zh: 律文，子賊殺傷毆父母，梟首，罵詈，棄市，謀殺夫之父母，亦棄市。

translations.literal: The statutes provide: for a son who is a villain, killing, wounding, or beating parents—decapitation and display; reviling and cursing—execution in the marketplace; plotting to kill a husband's parents—also execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes provide: for a son who is a villain, killing, wounding, or beating parents—decapitation and display; reviling and cursing—execution in the marketplace; plotting to kill a husband's parents—also execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 值赦，免刑補冶。

translations.literal: When an amnesty is in force, capital punishment is remitted and the offender is conscripted to the ironworks.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty is in force, capital punishment is remitted and the offender is conscripted to the ironworks.

sentences.zh: 江陵罵母，母以之自裁，重於傷毆。

translations.literal: Jiangling reviled his mother, and his mother took her own life because of it—this is heavier than wounding or beating.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling reviled his mother, and his mother took her own life because of it—this is heavier than wounding or beating.

sentences.zh: 若同殺科，則疑重，用毆傷及罵科，則疑輕。

translations.literal: If treated under the statute for killing, it seems too heavy; if the statutes for wounding or reviling are applied, it seems too light.
translations.idiomatic: If treated under the statute for killing, it seems too heavy; if the statutes for wounding or reviling are applied, it seems too light.

sentences.zh: 制唯有打母，遇赦猶梟首，無罵母致死值赦之科。

translations.literal: The code has only the case of beating one's mother, where even under amnesty decapitation and display still apply; there is no statute for reviling one's mother to death under amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The code has only the case of beating one's mother, where even under amnesty decapitation and display still apply; there is no statute for reviling one's mother to death under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 淵之議曰：「夫題里逆心，而仁者不入，名且惡之，況乃人事。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi argued: "One whose neighborhood bears the mark of a villain's heart—even the humane will not enter; the name itself is detested, how much more the deed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi argued: "One whose neighborhood bears the mark of a villain's heart—even the humane will not enter; the name itself is detested, how much more the deed itself.

sentences.zh: 故毆傷呪詛，法所不原，詈之致盡，則理無可宥。

translations.literal: Therefore wounding, beating, and cursing are what the law does not pardon; when reviling leads to death, there is by principle no forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore wounding, beating, and cursing are what the law does not pardon; when reviling leads to death, there is by principle no forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 罰有從輕，蓋疑失善，求之文旨，非此之謂。

translations.literal: That penalties may be reduced when doubt favors mercy is because one fears losing what is good; sought in the text of the law, this case is not of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: That penalties may be reduced when doubt favors mercy is because one fears losing what is good; sought in the text of the law, this case is not of that kind.

sentences.zh: 江陵雖值赦恩，故合梟首。

translations.literal: Although Jiangling encountered an amnesty, he should therefore be decapitated and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jiangling encountered an amnesty, he should therefore be decapitated and displayed.

sentences.zh: 婦本以義，愛非天屬，黃之所恨，情不在吳，原死補冶，有允正法。

translations.literal: A wife is bound by righteousness, not by natural kinship; what Huang resented was not directed at Wu. To remit death and conscript to the ironworks accords with the proper law.
translations.idiomatic: A wife is bound by righteousness, not by natural kinship; what Huang resented was not directed at Wu. To remit death and conscript to the ironworks accords with the proper law.

sentences.zh: 」詔如淵之議，吳免棄市。

translations.literal: " An edict followed Yuanzhi's opinion; Wu was spared execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Yuanzhi's opinion; Wu was spared execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 羊玄保

translations.literal: Yang Xuanbao
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao

sentences.zh: 羊玄保，太山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanbao was a native of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao was a native of Nancheng in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai had been Director of the Department of Justice in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai had been Director of the Department of Justice in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父綏，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Sui had been Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui had been Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄保起家楚臺太常博士，遭母憂，服闕，右將軍何無忌、前將軍諸葛長民俱板為參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: Xuanbao began his career as erudite of the Grand Ceremonial on the Chu court; he entered mourning for his mother, and when mourning ended, General of the Right He Wuji and General of the Front Zhuge Changmin both summoned him as military aide, but he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao began his career as erudite of the Grand Ceremonial on the Chu court. After mourning for his mother ended, General of the Right He Wuji and General of the Front Zhuge Changmin both summoned him as military aide, but he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 除臨安令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Magistrate of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之舉為高祖鎮軍參軍，庫部郎，永世令。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi recommended him as military aide on Gaozu's Pacification Army staff, as Director of the Storehouses, and as Magistrate of Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi recommended him as military aide on Gaozu's Pacification Army staff, as Director of the Storehouses, and as Magistrate of Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 復為高祖太尉參軍，轉主簿，丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He again served as military aide on Gaozu's Grand Commandant staff, then became chief clerk and Assistant in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as military aide on Gaozu's Grand Commandant staff, then became chief clerk and Assistant in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，入為尚書右丞，轉左丞，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under Shaodi, he entered the Masters of Writing as Right Assistant, then Left Assistant, and Chief Clerk on the Right of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping under Shaodi, he entered the Masters of Writing as Right Assistant, then Left Assistant, and Chief Clerk on the Right of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 府公王弘甚知重之，謂左長史庾登之、吏部尚書王准之曰：「卿二賢明美朗識，會悟多通，然弘懿之望，故當共推羊也。

translations.literal: The Duke of the Domain, Wang Hong, valued him highly and said to Chief Clerk on the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You two are brilliant, clear-sighted, and broadly capable, yet in the expectation of great virtue, it is Yang whom we should jointly advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of the Domain, Wang Hong, valued him highly and said to Chief Clerk on the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You two are brilliant, clear-sighted, and broadly capable, yet in the expectation of great virtue, it is Yang whom we should jointly advance.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，入為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he entered the palace as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he entered the palace as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 善弈棊，棊品第三，太祖與賭郡戲，勝，以補宣城太守。

translations.literal: He was skilled at chess; his chess rank was third. Taizu wagered commanderies in a game with him; Xuanbao won and was appointed to fill the post of Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at chess; his chess rank was third. Taizu wagered commanderies in a game with him; Xuanbao won and was appointed to fill the post of Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉式之為宣城，立吏民亡叛制，一人不禽，符伍里吏送州作部，若獲者賞位二階。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Shizhi was Administrator of Xuancheng, he had established a system for officials, clerks, and commoners who fled: if one person was not captured, the writ would bind the five-household unit and the district clerk would send him to the provincial convict labor corps; if captured, the captor was rewarded with two ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Shizhi was Administrator of Xuancheng, he had established a system for officials, clerks, and commoners who fled: if one person was not captured, the writ would bind the five-household unit and the district clerk would send him to the provincial convict labor corps; if captured, the captor was rewarded with two ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 玄保以為非宜，陳之曰：「臣伏尋亡叛之由，皆出於窮逼，未有足以推存而樂為此者也。

translations.literal: Xuanbao held this unsuitable and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has examined the causes of flight: all arise from desperate poverty; there has never been anyone with enough to live on who delighted in doing this.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao held this unsuitable and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has examined the causes of flight: all arise from desperate poverty; there has never been anyone with enough to live on who delighted in doing this.

sentences.zh: 今立殊制，於事為苦。

translations.literal: To establish a special system now would make the matter bitter in practice.
translations.idiomatic: To establish a special system now would make the matter bitter in practice.

sentences.zh: 臣聞苦節不可貞，懼致流弊。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that harsh ordinances cannot be maintained; I fear this will lead to abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that harsh ordinances cannot be maintained; I fear this will lead to abuses.

sentences.zh: 昔龔遂譬民於亂繩，緩之然後可理，黃覇以寬和為用，不以嚴刻為先。

translations.literal: In former times Gong Sui likened the people to tangled rope: only when it is loosened can it be governed; Huang Ba took leniency and harmony as his method and did not put severity first.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Gong Sui likened the people to tangled rope: only when it is loosened can it be governed; Huang Ba took leniency and harmony as his method and did not put severity first.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以謂單身逃役，便為盡戶。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that when a single person flees corvée, the whole household is treated as having fled.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant foolishly holds that when a single person flees corvée, the whole household is treated as having fled.

sentences.zh: 今一人不測，坐者甚多，既憚重負，各為身計，牽挽逃竄，必致繁滋。

translations.literal: Now if one person flees without warning, many are implicated; fearing heavy burdens, each plans for himself, dragging and pulling one another into flight—this will surely multiply the evil.
translations.idiomatic: If a single person flees without warning, many are implicated. Fearing heavy burdens, each plans for himself, dragging others into flight—this will surely multiply the harm.

sentences.zh: 又能禽獲叛身，類非謹惜，既無堪能，坐陵勞吏，名器虛假，所妨實多，將階級不足供賞，服勤無以自勸。

translations.literal: Those who can capture fugitives are mostly not men of scruple; lacking real ability, they sit atop and bully the laboring clerks. Titles and offices are falsely claimed, and the harm is truly great: soon the ranks of reward will not suffice, and diligent service will have no way to encourage itself.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture fugitives are mostly not scrupulous men. Lacking real ability, they bully the laboring clerks. Titles and offices are falsely claimed, and the harm is great: soon the ranks of reward will not suffice, and diligent service will have no way to encourage itself.

sentences.zh: 又尋此制，施一邦而已，若其是邪，則應與天下為一，若其非邪，亦不宜獨行一郡。

translations.literal: Again, when one examines this system, it was applied in one commandery only. If it is right, it should be one with the realm; if it is wrong, it should not be carried out alone in one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Again, this system was applied in one commandery only. If it is right, it should apply throughout the realm; if it is wrong, it should not be carried out alone in one commandery.

sentences.zh: 民離憂患，其弊將甚。

translations.literal: When the people are torn from their cares and troubles, the harm will be very great.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are torn from their cares and troubles, the harm will be very great.

sentences.zh: 臣忝守所職，懼難遵用，致率管穴，冒以陳聞。

translations.literal: Your servant, holding the office entrusted to him, fears difficulty in carrying it out, and therefore ventures from his narrow learning to offer this report.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, holding the office entrusted to him, fears difficulty in carrying it out, and therefore ventures from his narrow learning to offer this report.

sentences.zh: 」由此此制得停。

translations.literal: " Thereby this system was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby this system was halted.

sentences.zh: 玄保在郡一年，為廷尉。

translations.literal: Xuanbao had been in the commandery one year when he was made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao had been in the commandery one year when he was made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 數月，遷尚書吏部郎，御史中丞，衡陽王義季右軍長史、南東海太守，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Several months later he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, Censor-in-Chief, chief administrator on the Right Army staff of the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, and Administrator of Eastern Donghai, with the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, Censor-in-Chief, chief administrator on the Right Army staff of the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, and Administrator of Eastern Donghai, with the additional title General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 入為都官尚書、左衞將軍，加給事中，丹陽尹，會稽太守。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments, General of the Left Guard with added Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Governor of Danyang, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments, General of the Left Guard with added Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Governor of Danyang, and Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 又徙吳郡太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as Administrator of Wu commandery with salary at two thousand bushels, middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred as Administrator of Wu commandery with salary at two thousand bushels, middle grade.

sentences.zh: 太祖以玄保廉素寡欲，故頻授名郡。

translations.literal: Taizu, because Xuanbao was frugal, plain, and of few desires, repeatedly gave him famous commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, because Xuanbao was frugal, plain, and of few desires, repeatedly gave him famous commanderies.

sentences.zh: 為政雖無幹績，而去後常見思。

translations.literal: Though his administration showed no striking achievement, after he left he was often remembered with affection.
translations.idiomatic: Though his administration showed no striking achievement, after he left he was often remembered with affection.

sentences.zh: 不營財利，處家儉薄。

translations.literal: He did not pursue profit and kept his household spare.
translations.idiomatic: He did not pursue profit and kept his household spare.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗曰：「人仕宦非唯須才，然亦須運命，每有好官缺，我未嘗不先憶羊玄保。」

translations.literal: Taizu once said: "In entering office, one needs not only talent but also fate. Whenever a good post falls vacant, I never fail to think first of Yang Xuanbao."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once said: "In entering office, one needs not only talent but also fate. Whenever a good post falls vacant, I never fail to think first of Yang Xuanbao."

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，為吏部尚書，領國子祭酒，尋加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the malefactor usurped the throne by regicide, Xuanbao became Minister of Personnel and Chancellor of the National University, and soon was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the malefactor usurped the throne by regicide, Xuanbao became Minister of Personnel and Chancellor of the National University, and soon was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 及世祖入討，朝野多南奔，劭集羣僚，橫刀怒曰：「卿等便可去矣！

translations.literal: When Shizu marched in to punish him, court and countryside mostly fled south. Shao assembled the officials, drew his sword, and said in anger: "You may all leave now!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu marched in to punish him, court and countryside mostly fled south. Shao assembled the officials, drew his sword, and said in anger: "You may all leave now!"

sentences.zh: 」眾戰懼莫敢言，玄保容色不異，徐曰：「臣以死奉朝。

translations.literal: " The crowd trembled in fear and none dared speak. Xuanbao's expression did not change, and he said slowly: "Your servant will serve the court with his death."
translations.idiomatic: The crowd trembled in fear and none dared speak. Xuanbao's expression did not change, and he said slowly: "Your servant will serve the court with his death."

sentences.zh: 」劭乃解。

translations.literal: " Shao then relented.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then relented.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以為散騎常侍，領崇憲衞尉。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Xuanbao was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and put in charge of the Chongxian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Xuanbao was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and put in charge of the Chongxian Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 又以謹敬見知，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Again, because of his reverence and respect he was recognized and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because of his reverence and respect he was recognized and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 大明初，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daming era he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daming era he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷散騎常侍，特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Special Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 玄保自少至老，謹於祭奠，四時珍新，未得祠薦者，口不妄嘗。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Xuanbao was scrupulous in sacrifice; seasonal delicacies—what had not yet been offered in the rites he would not taste at random.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Xuanbao was scrupulous in sacrifice. Seasonal delicacies that had not yet been offered in the rites he would not taste at random.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，時年九十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died, aged ninety-four.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ding.

sentences.zh: 子戎，有才氣，而輕薄少行檢，玄保嘗云：「此兒必亡我家。

translations.literal: His son Rong had talent but was frivolous and short on conduct; Xuanbao once said: "This boy will ruin my house.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong had talent but was frivolous and short on conduct. Xuanbao once said: "This boy will ruin my house.

sentences.zh: 」官至通直郎。

translations.literal: " He reached the post of Director of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of Director of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 與王僧達謗議時政，賜死。

translations.literal: With Wang Sengda he slandered and discussed current affairs and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Sengda he slandered and discussed current affairs and was granted death.

sentences.zh: 死後世祖引見玄保，玄保謝曰：「臣無日磾之明，以此上負。

translations.literal: Afterward Shizu summoned Xuanbao and Xuanbao apologized, saying: "Your servant lacks the discernment of Ri Di and has failed his superiors on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Shizu summoned Xuanbao and Xuanbao apologized, saying: "Your servant lacks the discernment of Ri Di and has failed his superiors on this account.

sentences.zh: 」上美其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words.

sentences.zh: 戎二弟，太祖並賜名，曰咸，曰粲。

translations.literal: Rong's two younger brothers were both given names by Taizu: Xian and Can.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's two younger brothers were both given names by Taizu: Xian and Can.

sentences.zh: 謂玄保曰：「欲令卿二子有林下正始餘風。」

translations.literal: He said to Xuanbao: "I wish your two sons to have the remaining flavor of the pure style of the Zhengshi era in the forests and hills."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Xuanbao: "I wish your two sons to have the remaining flavor of the pure style of the Zhengshi era in the forests and hills."

sentences.zh: 玄保既善棊，而何尚之亦雅好棊。

translations.literal: Xuanbao was skilled at chess, and He Shangzhi also loved chess deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao was skilled at chess, and He Shangzhi also loved chess deeply.

sentences.zh: 吳郡褚胤，年七歲，入高品。

translations.literal: Chu Yin of Wu commandery, at seven years of age, entered the high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yin of Wu commandery, at seven years of age, entered the high rank.

translations.idiomatic: Now let it be revised anew and five articles established.

translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yizhou Liu Yu had earlier been General of the Right Guard and, with staff major He Jimu on the domain office, did not get along.

translations.idiomatic: Jimu was favored by the Minister of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Pingping, Hong, and repeatedly slandered Yu to Hong.

translations.idiomatic: When Yu went out as Inspector of Yizhou, he seized a scholar's wife as concubine; Hong had Yang Xi impeach him, and Yu was dismissed from office; Yu hated Xi to the teeth.

sentences.zh: 有門生謝元伯往來希間，瑀令訪訊被免之由。

translations.idiomatic: A student, Xie Yuanbo, came and went with Xi; Yu had him inquire into the reason for dismissal.

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era he was consultation army aide on the staff of the Prince of Shi'an, Zizhen, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era he was consultation army aide on the staff of the Prince of Shi'an, Zizhen, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，出為寧朔將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 希初請女夫鎮北中兵參軍蕭惠徽為長史，帶南海太守，太宗不許。

translations.literal: Xi first requested his son-in-law, Army Aide of the Pacify-the-North Army Xiao Huizhen, as chief administrator with concurrent Administrator of Nanhai; Taizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi first requested his son-in-law, Army Aide of the Pacify-the-North Army Xiao Huizhen, as chief administrator with concurrent Administrator of Nanhai; Taizong did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 又請為東莞太守。

translations.literal: He again requested to be Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested to be Administrator of Dongguan.

translations.idiomatic: After Xi reached his post, Chief Administrator and Administrator of Nanhai Lu Fazhen died in office; Xi again requested Huizhen to fill the post.

translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Xi is of a humble gate and cold stock, unknown for generations, frivolous and full of faults, all plainly shown in his successive offices.

translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Wanzhou and Liu Sizu had seized Guangzhou by force—the matter is in the Biography of Deng Wan.

translations.idiomatic: Taizong made Wanzhou Infantry Commandant with added General Who Pacifies the North, acting Inspector of Guangzhou.

translations.literal: After Xi arrived, Wanzhou and the others all harbored divergent designs; Xi executed them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi arrived, Wanzhou and the others all harbored divergent designs; Xi executed them.

sentences.zh: 希以沛郡劉思道行晉康太守，領軍伐俚。

translations.literal: Xi sent Liu Sidao of Pei commandery to act as Administrator of Jinkang and lead the army to campaign against the Li.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent Liu Sidao of Pei commandery to act as Administrator of Jinkang and lead the army to campaign against the Li.

sentences.zh: 思道違節度，失利，希遣收之。

translations.literal: Sidao violated orders and failed; Xi sent men to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao violated orders and failed; Xi sent men to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 思道不受命，率所領攻州，希遣平越長史鄒琰於朝亭拒戰，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: Sidao would not accept the command and led his followers to attack the province; Xi sent Zou Yan, chief administrator of Pacify-Yue, to resist at Chaoting; the army was defeated and Yan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao would not accept the command and led his followers to attack the province; Xi sent Zou Yan, chief administrator of Pacify-Yue, to resist at Chaoting; the army was defeated and Yan was killed.

sentences.zh: 思道進攻州城，司馬鄒嗣之拒之西門，戰敗又死。

translations.literal: Sidao pressed the attack on the provincial city; staff major Zou Sizhi resisted him at the west gate, was defeated, and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao pressed the attack on the provincial city; staff major Zou Sizhi resisted him at the west gate, was defeated, and also died.

sentences.zh: 希踰城走，思道獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Xi fled over the wall; Sidao captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fled over the wall; Sidao captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 府參軍鄒曼率數十人襲思道，已得入城，力不敵，又敗。

translations.literal: Staff aide Zou Man led several dozen men to strike at Sidao; he had already entered the city but lacked strength and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Staff aide Zou Man led several dozen men to strike at Sidao; he had already entered the city but lacked strength and was again defeated.

sentences.zh: 東莞太守蕭惠徽率郡文武千餘人攻思道，戰敗，又見殺。

translations.literal: Administrator of Dongguan Xiao Huizhen led more than a thousand men of the commandery civil and military to attack Sidao, was defeated, and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Dongguan Xiao Huizhen led more than a thousand men of the commandery civil and military to attack Sidao, was defeated, and was also killed.

sentences.zh: 時龍驤將軍陳伯紹率軍伐俚，還擊思道，定之。

translations.literal: At the time General of the Flying Dragon Army Chen Bozhao was campaigning against the Li and, on his return, struck Sidao and settled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time General of the Flying Dragon Army Chen Bozhao was campaigning against the Li and, on his return, struck Sidao and settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 贈希輔國將軍，惠徽中書郎，嗣之越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously Xi was granted General Who Assists the State, Huizhen Director of the Secretariat, and Sizhi Commandant of the Rapid Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Xi was granted General Who Assists the State, Huizhen Director of the Secretariat, and Sizhi Commandant of the Rapid Horse.

sentences.zh: 希子崇字伯遠，尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: Xi's son Chong, style name Boyuan, was Director of Guests in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Chong, style name Boyuan, was Director of Guests in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; his grief and ruin exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother; his grief and ruin exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 及聞廣州亂，即日便徒跣出新亭，不能步涉，頓伏江渚。

translations.literal: When he heard of the turmoil in Guangzhou, that very day he went out barefoot to Xinting and could not walk; he collapsed on the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the turmoil in Guangzhou, that very day he went out barefoot to Xinting and could not walk; he collapsed on the river bank.

sentences.zh: 門義以小船致之，於是進路。

translations.literal: A household retainer brought him in a small boat, and only then did he go forward.
translations.idiomatic: A household retainer brought him in a small boat, and only then did he go forward.

sentences.zh: 父葬畢，不勝哀，卒。

translations.literal: After his father's burial was complete, he could not bear his grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's burial was complete, he could not bear his grief and died.

translations.idiomatic: Shen Tanqing

translations.idiomatic: Shen Tanqing was a man of Wukang in Wuxing and a cousin of Palace Attendant Huaiwen.

translations.idiomatic: His father Fa had been Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and died young; Wang Shaozhi, Administrator of Wuxing, composed a dirge for him.

translations.literal: At first Tanqing was summoned as chief clerk, provincial aide, western bureau chief clerk, and chief clerk on the Rear Army and Pacification Army staffs of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing was first summoned as chief clerk, provincial aide, western bureau chief clerk, and chief clerk on the Rear Army and Pacification Army staffs of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀致稱，本縣令諸葛闡之公解言上。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; his grief and ruin won praise, and the magistrate of his home county, Zhuge Chanzhi, reported it upward in a public memorial of release.
translations.idiomatic: When he mourned his mother, his grief and ruin won praise, and the magistrate of his home county, Zhuge Chanzhi, reported it upward in a public memorial.

sentences.zh: 服釋，復為主簿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again became chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he again became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 義欣又請為鎮軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: Yixin again requested him as consultation army aide on the Pacification Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin again requested him as consultation army aide on the Pacification Army staff.

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Yuhang, was promoted to chief clerk of the Minister of Education, recording army aide on the Grand Commandant staff of the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and Right Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Magistrate of Yuhang, was promoted to chief clerk of the Minister of Education, recording army aide on the Grand Commandant staff of the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and Right Assistant in the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: In years of flood and drought, Tanqing proposed establishing ever-normal granaries to relieve the people's urgency; Taizu accepted his words, but the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In years of flood and drought, Tanqing proposed establishing ever-normal granaries to relieve the people's urgency. Taizu accepted his advice, but the matter was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 領本邑中正，少府，揚州治中從事史，始興王濬衞軍長史。

translations.literal: He headed the chief rectifier of his home district, Director of the Palace Parks, Senior Clerk attached to the chief administrator of Yangzhou, and chief administrator on the Guard Army staff of the Prince of Shixing, Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the chief rectifier of his home district, Director of the Palace Parks, Senior Clerk attached to the chief administrator of Yangzhou, and chief administrator on the Guard Army staff of the Prince of Shixing, Jun.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，世祖入討，劭遣曇慶還東募人，安東將軍隨王誕收付永興縣獄，久之，被原。

translations.literal: When the malefactor usurped by regicide and Shizu marched in to punish him, Shao sent Tanqing back east to recruit men. General Who Pacifies the East, the Prince of Sui, Dan, had him taken and held in the prison of Yongxing county; after a long time he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the malefactor usurped by regicide and Shizu marched in to punish him, Shao sent Tanqing back east to recruit men. General Who Pacifies the East, the Prince of Sui, Dan, had him taken and held in the prison of Yongxing county. After a long time he was pardoned.

translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended the throne, Tanqing was appointed chief administrator on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Donghai, Hui. He entered the Masters of Writing as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, became chief administrator on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and Administrator of Southern Donghai and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，督徐兗二州及梁郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he supervised military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery, as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he supervised military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery, as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時殿中員外將軍裴景仁助戍彭城，本傖人，多悉戎荒事。

translations.literal: At the time Supernumerary General of the Palace Army Pei Jingren was assisting in the defense of Pengcheng; he was originally a tribal man and knew much of frontier and wilderness affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Supernumerary General of the Palace Army Pei Jingren was assisting in the defense of Pengcheng. He was originally of tribal origin and knew much of frontier and wilderness affairs.

sentences.zh: 曇慶使撰秦記十卷，敍苻氏僭偽本末，其書傳於世。

translations.literal: Tanqing had him compile ten juan of Records of Qin, narrating the rise and fall of the Fu clan's usurpation; the book circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing had him compile ten juan of Records of Qin, narrating the rise and fall of the Fu clan's usurpation. The book circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 明年，復徵為左衞將軍，加給事中，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned as General of the Left Guard with added Supernumerary Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again summoned as General of the Left Guard with added Supernumerary Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷祠部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其年，卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 時年五十七。

translations.literal: He was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈本官。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted his former office.

sentences.zh: 曇慶謹實清正，所莅有稱績。

translations.literal: Tanqing was scrupulous, solid, and upright; in every post he held he won praised achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing was scrupulous, solid, and upright; in every post he held he won praised achievement.

sentences.zh: 常謂子弟曰：「吾處世無才能，政圖作大老子耳。

translations.literal: He often told his sons and younger brothers: "I have no talent in dealing with the world; I only aim to be a great old man.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his sons and younger brothers: "I have no talent in dealing with the world; I only aim to be a great old man.

sentences.zh: 」世以長者稱之。

translations.literal: " The age called him an elder.
translations.idiomatic: The age called him an elder.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江南之為國盛矣，雖南包象浦，西括邛山，至於外奉貢賦，內充府實，止於荊、揚二州。

translations.literal: The historian says: As a state the southland was prosperous indeed. Though it embraced Xiangpu in the south and Qiongshan in the west, as for outwardly presenting tribute and inwardly filling the treasuries, this extended only to Jing and Yang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: As a state the southland was prosperous indeed. Though it embraced Xiangpu in the south and Qiongshan in the west, outward tribute and inward revenue extended only to Jing and Yang provinces.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏以來，民戶彫秏，荊楚四戰之地，五達之郊，井邑殘亡，萬不餘一也。

translations.literal: Since the Han house, households were worn away; Jing and Chu were a land of four battles and a crossroads of five roads—market towns were ruined and not one in ten thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han house, households were worn away. Jing and Chu were a land of four battles and a crossroads of five roads—market towns were ruined and not one in ten thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 自義熙十一年司馬休之外奔，至于元嘉末，三十有九載，兵車勿用，民不外勞，役寬務簡，氓庶繁息，至餘糧栖畝，戶不夜扃，蓋東西之極盛也。

translations.literal: From the eleventh year of Yixi, when Sima Xiuzhi fled abroad, to the end of Yuanjia—thirty-nine years—chariots and weapons were not used and the people were not worn by external labor; corvée was light and affairs simple, and the common folk multiplied. Grain lay surplus in the fields and households did not bar their doors at night—this was the utmost flourishing of east and west.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh year of Yixi, when Sima Xiuzhi fled abroad, to the end of Yuanjia—thirty-nine years—chariots and weapons were not used and the people were not worn by external labor. Corvée was light and affairs simple, and the common folk multiplied. Grain lay surplus in the fields and households did not bar their doors at night—this was the utmost flourishing of east and west.

sentences.zh: 既揚部分析，境極江南，考之漢域，惟丹陽會稽而已。

translations.literal: Once the Yang region was divided and analyzed, the border reached the utmost southland; measured against Han domains, only Danyang and Kuaiji remained.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yang region was divided and analyzed, the border reached the utmost southland. Measured against Han domains, only Danyang and Kuaiji remained.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏遷流，迄於太元之世，百許年中，無風塵之警，區域之內，晏如也。

translations.literal: From the Jin relocation of the court until the Taixuan era, for some hundred years there was no alarm of war; within the region, all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin relocation of the court until the Taixuan era, for some hundred years there was no alarm of war. Within the region, all was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩寇亂，殲亡事極，自此以至大明之季，年踰六紀，民戶繁育，將曩時一矣。

translations.literal: When Sun En's raids brought ruin to the extreme, from then until the Daming era more than six decades passed, and households multiplied until they nearly equaled former times.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En's raids brought ruin to the extreme, from then until the Daming era more than six decades passed, and households multiplied until they nearly equaled former times.

sentences.zh: 地廣野豐，民勤本業，一歲或稔，則數郡忘飢。

translations.literal: The land was broad and the fields rich; the people were diligent in their basic occupations. When one year brought a good harvest, several commanderies forgot hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The land was broad and the fields rich; the people were diligent in their basic occupations. When one year brought a good harvest, several commanderies forgot hunger.

sentences.zh: 會土帶海傍湖，良疇亦數十萬頃，膏腴上地，畝直一金，鄠、杜之間，不能比也。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji region borders the sea and adjoins lakes; good fields also number several hundred thousand qing. On rich upper soil a mu is worth a gold piece—the lands between E and Du cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji region borders the sea and adjoins lakes; good fields also number several hundred thousand qing. On rich upper soil a mu is worth a gold piece—the lands between E and Du cannot compare.

sentences.zh: 荊城跨南楚之富，揚部有全吳之沃，魚鹽𣏌梓之利，充仞八方，絲綿布帛之饒，覆衣天下。

translations.literal: Jing city spans the wealth of southern Chu; the Yang region holds the fertility of all Wu. The profit of fish, salt, and timber fills the eight directions; the abundance of silk, cotton, and cloth covers the realm in dress.
translations.idiomatic: Jing city spans the wealth of southern Chu; the Yang region holds the fertility of all Wu. The profit of fish, salt, and timber fills the eight directions; the abundance of silk, cotton, and cloth covers the realm in dress.

sentences.zh: 而田家作苦，役難利薄，亘歲從務，無或一日非農，而經稅橫賦之資，養生送死之具，莫不咸出於此。

translations.literal: Yet farming families labor bitterly; corvée is hard and profit thin. Through the year they follow their tasks, not a day without farming—and the funds for regular taxes and levies, and the means to sustain life and send off the dead, all come from this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet farming families labor bitterly; corvée is hard and profit thin. Through the year they follow their tasks, not a day without farming—and the funds for regular taxes and levies, and the means to sustain life and send off the dead, all come from this alone.

sentences.zh: 穰歲糶賤，糶賤則稼苦；

translations.literal: In a bumper year grain is sold cheap; when grain is cheap, farming is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: In a bumper year grain is sold cheap; when grain is cheap, farming is bitter.

sentences.zh: 饑年糴貴，糴貴則商倍。

translations.literal: In a famine year grain is bought dear; when grain is dear, merchants double.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year grain is bought dear; when grain is dear, merchants double their gains.

sentences.zh: 常平之議，行於漢世。

translations.literal: The proposal for ever-normal granaries was carried out in the Han era.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal for ever-normal granaries was carried out in the Han era.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，東土潦浸，民命棘矣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia the eastern lands were inundated; the people's lives were desperate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia the eastern lands were inundated; the people's lives were desperate.

sentences.zh: 太祖省費減用，開倉廩以振之，病而不凶，蓋此力也。

translations.literal: Taizu reduced expenses and opened the granaries to relieve them; sickness but not disaster—this was largely his doing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reduced expenses and opened the granaries to relieve them. There was sickness but not disaster—this was largely his doing.

sentences.zh: 大明之末，積旱成災，雖敝同往困，而救非昔主，所以病未半古，死已倍之，并命比室，口減過半。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming, drought piled up into disaster. Though the distress matched past hardship, the relief was not like rulers of old; thus sickness did not reach half the ancients' level, yet deaths already doubled. Deaths in the same household, mouths reduced by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daming, drought piled up into disaster. Though the distress matched past hardship, the relief was not like rulers of old. Sickness did not reach half the ancients' level, yet deaths already doubled—deaths in the same household, mouths reduced by more than half.

sentences.zh: 若常平之計，興於中年，遂切扶患，或不至是。

translations.literal: If the ever-normal plan had been raised in mid-era and applied directly to support the afflicted, it might not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: If the ever-normal plan had been raised in mid-era and applied directly to support the afflicted, it might not have come to this.

sentences.zh: 若籠以平價，則官苦民優，議屈當時，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: If grain were controlled at a fair price, the state would suffer and the people benefit; the proposal was defeated in its time—largely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: If grain were controlled at a fair price, the state would suffer and the people benefit. The proposal was defeated in its time—largely for this reason.
